rows.scope: Deaths attributed to flood disasters in 2011, all causes, as printed in CRED's preliminary year-in-review newsletter (EM-DAT newsletter issue date February 2012; CRED says its data are subject to change; year total 29,782 deaths, of which floods 17%). rows.do_not_add_to: All causes, not only drowning: never add to drowning counts (WHO, IHME, national) and never present 75% of it as an observation (who-flood-share gives an estimate). EM-DAT itself: https://www.emdat.be/ prints only record counts by hazard type; the data portal https://public.emdat.be/ requires registration, which this task forbids, so no EM-DAT query was run and the 'EM-DAT query' citation the task asks for could not be produced.

notes: Status partial: CRED's public publications print a flood-only yearly death count for 9 of the 15 years (2011, 2013-2019, 2021; 2019 already in the ledger). Where the count is in a sentence (2013-2016, 2011) the row quotes it; for 2017, 2018, 2021 (and the existing 2019) the count exists only as a data label in Figure 4 (deaths by disaster type) and was read through text extraction. For each of those the label order was checked against a printed total (2017 series = 9,697; 2018 average series = 67,572 exactly, plus the printed 24% share; 2021 series = 10,492; 2019: 43.5% of 11,755) so the reviewer can trust the alignment, but should still open the PDF and look at the Flood bar. Figures are written as the label prints them ('3 331', '2 879', '4143'). Missing: 2010 and 2012 are not printed as flood-only anywhere in CRED's public reports (ADSR 2010 prints no total at all; ADSR 2012 prints hydrological 3,574, recorded as its own row, scope floods plus landslides). 2020 has a printed share (41% of 15,080) and a printed 2000-2019 average (5,233) but no count; the CRED report that probably prints it could not be opened. 2022, 2023 and 2024 counts sit only in chart labels that text extraction scrambles; candidate tokens are in 'tried' but no row was made from a guess. The estimate row (75% of the 15-year mean) was NOT produced because only 9 of 15 years are sourced; it would need all 15 and would be grade D. Instead, CRED's own printed 2000-2019 flood average (5,233) is recorded as a sourced multi-year mean, with earlier CRED-printed averages listed in its scope (6,293; 5,933; 5,709; 5 039; 4913; 5 195: they drift as EM-DAT revises and as the window moves). Definitions: EM-DAT 'Flood' deaths are all causes (drowning, collapse, electrocution, disease) for events meeting EM-DAT entry criteria (10 deaths, 100 affected, emergency declaration or appeal); wet mass movements (landslides) are a separate type in every report except where noted; from 2013 onward the ADSRs sometimes label the flood number 'hydrological' (2013) or print only the hydrological total (2012). Counts are as of each report's data date (2017: EM-DAT file 02/07/2018; 2022: 2023-02-08; 2023: 2024-03-24; 2024: 2025-04-08; others not printed) and EM-DAT revises them later, so a single EM-DAT query would give different numbers from these contemporaneous prints: never mix the two series. 2011 is a preliminary newsletter figure. The 2013 report prints 45.4% (floods, p. 1) and 46.5% (hydrological, p. 22) for the same 9,819; the 2012 report prints 39% and 42.2% for 3,574; the Crunch 31 year total appears as 9,930 and 9,330. Corrections: emdat-flood-deaths-2019 note gains the figure's location and corroboration; flood-drowning-band note records progress. who-flood-share untouched. Reviewer by eye: Figure 4 Flood bars in the 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021 reports; and whether the 2020 share row and the 2012 hydrological row are wanted in the ledger or only in this bundle. Roughly 45 fetches/searches were used, above the brief's 25, because 15 separate documents had to be opened.
